questions.q: Why does `userIdentity.accessKeyId` matter more during an investigation than just knowing the IAM username involved?
options: It ties every action back to the specific credential that was actually leaked, which matters when a user has more than one access key
It shows the dollar cost of each API call
It is only populated for root account activity
It replaces the need for sourceIPAddress entirely
questions.explain: A single IAM user can have multiple access keys; accessKeyId pinpoints exactly which one was used for a given action, which is essential when only one of several keys was leaked.

questions.q: Why are CloudTrail data events (like S3 object-level GetObject/PutObject) off by default?
options: AWS disabled them permanently for compliance reasons
They only work in GovCloud regions
Because of their volume and cost, so they must be deliberately enabled on buckets holding sensitive data to prove which objects were actually touched
They are automatically replaced by CloudTrail Insights
questions.explain: Data events log every object-level operation and can be extremely high-volume; they're off by default and need to be turned on specifically where proving object-level access matters.

questions.q: What does CloudTrail Insights add that a simple rule-based CloudTrail alert would miss?
options: It encrypts CloudTrail logs automatically
Unsupervised anomaly detection on unusual VOLUMES of API calls, such as a sudden burst of DescribeInstances calls
It blocks suspicious API calls in real time before they execute
It replaces the need for a multi-region trail
questions.explain: Insights is built specifically to flag unusual call-volume patterns that wouldn't trip a simple named-event alert, which is useful for catching enumeration bursts.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Azure Activity Log and Azure AD sign-in logs?
options: They are two names for exactly the same data
Sign-in logs only exist for Global Administrators
Activity Log has no correlationId field, unlike sign-in logs

Activity Log records control-plane operations against Azure Resource Manager, while sign-in logs record a completely separate stream of authentication events, including Conditional Access outcomes and risk level
questions.explain: Treating 'the Azure logs' as one source is a common mistake — Activity Log covers ARM control-plane operations, while sign-in logs are a separate authentication-event stream with their own Conditional Access and risk-level data.

questions.q: In a real cross-platform investigation, where would you actually see an Application Administrator adding a new secret to a service principal they didn't create?
options: CloudTrail Insights
The AWS GuardDuty console
The Azure AD audit log, which covers directory changes like new app registrations and added service principal credentials
Nowhere — this action is not logged in Azure
questions.explain: Directory-level changes such as adding a credential to an existing service principal are captured in the Azure AD audit log, a separate stream from both the Activity Log and sign-in logs.
